findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'Retry and timeout on Bedrock' mechanism claim with what actually ships: either specify the Bedrock builder to thread a botocore.config.Config (retries + read/connect timeout derived from llm_retry_max_attempts/timeout_s, per the ratified design on bug 61d8, i.e. BedrockProvider(bedrock_client=...) not the plan's aws_read_timeout kwarg), OR explicitly downgrade the plan's parity/'full fidelity' language to state that Bedrock retry/timeout parity is deferred (bug 61d8) and that S6 does not yet measure it.
evidence: Plan asserts: 'the Bedrock builder constructs its client with botocore.config.Config(retries={"max_attempts": cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts, "mode": "adaptive"}) and passes it as BedrockProvider(bedrock_client=...)' and 'BedrockProvider(aws_read_timeout=cfg.timeout_s, aws_connect_timeout=10.0)' → 'The retry-attempt count and the read timeout are thus driven by the SAME LLMConfig fields on both first-class providers, which is the parity S6 measures.'

Actual code: bedrock_model.py:101 `return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` — no botocore Config, no adaptive mode, no aws_read_timeout/aws_connect_timeout (also confirmed by the in-scope ADR 0059 §'the retry/timeout gap': the grep for botocore.config/aws_read_timeout 'returns nothing').

Plan's own resulting ADR 0059:860-865 records under 'Negative, and deliberately accepted': 'first_class does NOT currently mean retry/timeout parity. llm_retry_max_attempts and timeout_s do not reach Bedrock at all... Since production is Bedrock, the unconfigured path is the live one.'

Bug 61d8-ff23-8ee0-4289 (status in_progress, discovered_from the cutover) confirms 'an unmet intention, not a landed property' and that its Approach was 'not yet designed' when filed — the parity mechanism the plan presents as fact was undesigned.
The tenacity retry envelope + configured httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s) exist ONLY on the Anthropic path (anthropic_model.py:113-125, providers.py:219).
findings.finding: The plan's 'Retry and timeout on Bedrock' section presents a botocore-Config retry envelope and aws_read_timeout/aws_connect_timeout as the achieved mechanism that gives the first-class Bedrock tier retry/timeout parity ('driven by the SAME LLMConfig fields on both first-class providers, which is the parity S6 measures'), but this mechanism is not delivered: the Bedrock builder is a bare BedrockProvider(region_name=region) with no botocore Config, so llm_retry_max_attempts, llm_retry_max_wait_s, and timeout_s do not reach Bedrock at all — making the stated parity claim (and the 'full fidelity' first-class characterisation for the live production path) false as written.
findings.location: Plan §Approach, 'Retry and timeout on Bedrock' paragraph; scope item src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py / parity.py (S6)
scenarios: An operator on the Bedrock (production) path sets REBAR_LLM_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS or REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT to tune throttle handling; the knob is wired to nothing and silently has no effect.
S6 parity is asserted to 'measure' retry/timeout equality that the code does not implement, so a green S6 attestation does not evidence the property the plan claims for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the plan's assertion that the parity is achieved with the ratified design: build the boto3 client in build_bedrock_provider via session.client('bedrock-runtime', config=Config(retries={'max_attempts': cfg.llm_retry_max_attempts, 'mode': 'adaptive'}, connect_timeout=..., read_timeout=cfg.timeout_s)) and pass BedrockProvider(bedrock_client=...); note that llm_retry_max_wait_s has no botocore equivalent and is not mapped. If that work stays out of scope, restate the first-class tier as 'native fidelity for caching/structured-output/thinking; retry+timeout parity deferred to 61d8' and remove the 'the parity S6 measures' clause.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the environment precondition that the chosen default Bedrock model id must be model-access-enabled AND caching-effective in the PRODUCTION account/region (896586841071 / us-east-1), and require the caching/invokability probe to be re-run there before the no-fallback S8 cutover — not relied on from the us-east-2 account 5797…98 measurement.
evidence: Plan asserts: 'The native BedrockConverseModel path needs no proxy and supports prompt caching via BedrockModelSettings' and treats Bedrock caching as an implementable first-class capability.

S3 (2932) live measurement: 'us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5 … both report cache_read=0 AND cache_write=0 on both attempts, billing the full 4029 input tokens every call — no error, no warning. … Caching is MODEL-dependent and fails SILENTLY.'

S3 'IMPORTANT CORRECTION' comment: measurements were taken in account 5797…98 / us-east-2, but the project runs in account 896586841071 / us-east-1; 'DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID as shipped may not even be ENABLED in the project account — that must be verified before S8 cuts the production bot over to it with no fallback.'
T3 axis (c): environment preconditions — a platform-capability probe in the WRONG account/region is not a verification of the deployment environment.
findings.finding: The plan asserts native Bedrock prompt caching as a first-class capability and picks a default model (us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6), but states no environment precondition that the PRODUCTION AWS account/region must have that model enabled AND caching-effective — and Bedrock model access + prompt-cache effectiveness are per-account/per-region and can fail SILENTLY (full-price billing, no error) on a per-model basis.
findings.location: Approach — 'Retry and timeout on Bedrock…'/'Capability assertions verified…'; Acceptance Criteria (Bedrock cache-read AC and the S8 no-fallback cutover AC)
scenarios: S8 cuts the production review bot over to Bedrock with no direct-Anthropic fallback, but the chosen default model id is not enabled (or does not cache) in account 896586841071 / us-east-1.
Operators silently pay full input price on every call because the chosen model does not cache in the production region.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit precondition + a SPIKE-style gate to the Bedrock/S8 criteria: re-run the cache/invokability probe in 896586841071/us-east-1, confirm (a) the default id is invokable, (b) it reports non-zero cache_read on the second identical call there, and (c) the silent-zero-cache warning fires, BEFORE removing the direct-Anthropic fallback.

findings.suggested_fix: Either add e951 to the epic's child set (or fold the finalize.py producer edit into 343b), so parent AC7's producer→sidecar chain is fully owned within the roster rather than relying on a non-child prerequisite.
